project.objective: When and where did Anders Monsen marry Unna Halsteinsdatter, and what does the marriage record show?

questions.question: When and where did Anders Monsen (born 1759 in Håtuft, Meland, Hordaland, Norway; died 1821 in Åsebø, Manger, Hordaland) marry Unna Halsteinsdatter (born May 1745 in Hestdal, Hammer, Hordaland)?
questions.rationale: The tree links Anders and Unna as a couple but records no marriage fact for them. The marriage event is the single fact the objective names; its record content is what the answer will rest on, so the record itself is left to the research plan. The 1759 birth and 1821 death give a marriage window of roughly 1775 to 1821.

search_stop.justification: Wrapped up by the researcher before the remaining plan items were run. The marriage index record NW44-PM2 (Norway Marriages 1660-1926) gives 25 June 1786 at Hamre, Hordaland, with Anders Monsen (match 0.97) and Unna (match 0.90) linked to the subject and wife. The original Hamre register entry was not read: the image browse returned 403 Forbidden on every page tried (log_003), so the bride's name and the register wording rest on the index. Searches for children's baptisms and an earlier marriage of Unna were negative. The 1801 census gave one unadopted candidate. Burial, probate and the farm-history book were not searched because the researcher declined them. No civil registration existed for this period; the Hamre parish register is the vital record of the event. Stopped without a stop-gate value; no declaration made.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Conclusion

Anders Monsen (born 1759, Håtuft, Meland; died 1821, Åsebø, Manger) most likely married Unna Halsteinsdatter (born May 1745, Hestdal, Hammer) on 25 June 1786 in Hamre, Hordaland, Norway. Tier: probable. Form: summary.

## Evidence

The only record found is the index entry for Anders Monsen and Urna Halsteinsdr, dated 25 June 1786, in "Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926" (citation: "Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2 : Thu Oct 08 17:58:07 UTC 2026), Entry for Anders Monsen and Urna Halsteinsdr, 25 June 1786). It is a derivative source (an index of a church register). Its information about the event is primary, with the couple as the parties, and it states the date and place directly; the bride is named in the variant spelling 'Urna Halsteinsdr', the same patronymic as Unna Halsteinsdatter.

## Identity

The groom persona matches the tree's Anders Monsen (same_person 0.97) and the bride persona matches Unna Halsteinsdatter (0.90). Supporting this: Hamre is in the same county as his birth and death places and is the parish where Unna was christened (the Hamre clerical district included Meland and Hammer parishes), and the record names the very spouse the tree already joins him to. Unna would have been about 41 at a first marriage; an earlier marriage of hers was searched for and not found, so this is noted as unusual but not contradictory. The name Anders Monsen is common, so the spouse and place agreement carry the identity. No conflicts are registered.

## Limits

The original Hamre register entry could not be read (images returned 403 Forbidden), so the date, place and spellings rest on one index transcription, with no independent second source. Children's baptisms and the 1801 census gave no corroboration. The 'place' is the Hamre clerical district as the index gives it; the specific church within it is not shown. Unsearched records are listed in the search summary. The conclusion is well supported but rests on a single derivative source, so it is probable, not proved. Reading the original register entry, or a second independent record, would raise it.

quirks: Until 1885 Meland and Hammer (Hamre) parishes were both part of the same Hamre prestegjeld (clerical district), along with Alversund and Åsane with Salhus chapel — a marriage between a Meland groom and a Hammer-parish bride in 1750-1821 was very likely recorded in the SAME Hamre kirkebok, not two separate parish books. The FamilySearch Catalog entry 'Kirkebøker, 1677-1928' (Hamre prestegjeld, catalog #47267) is the single register series to search for both home parishes in this period; see also catalog #209228 (extract of christenings and marriages 1677-1826) and Digitalarkivet's 'Hamre/Alversund, Hamre, Hosanger, Meland, Mo, Seim Parish Church Records 1677-1750' and 'Hamre/Alversund, Hamre, Meland Parish Church Records 1750-1857' coverage groups.

Per the FamilySearch Wiki (Norway Church Records), couples were usually married in the BRIDE'S home parish — so search for the Anders Monsen/Unna Halsteinsdatter marriage under Hammer/Hamre (Unna's home parish, Hestdal) first, within the same Hamre prestegjeld register.

Norway Church Records page (FamilySearch Wiki): https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Church_Records — pre-1814 marriage entries vary in content (no fixed form); typically give bride/groom names, marriage date, residence, single/widowed status, occupations, and names of bondsmen (often fathers after ~1830s); a separate engagement (trolovelse) entry sometimes appears earlier in the register.

A 1677-1826 extract of christenings and marriages for Hamre exists at FamilySearch Catalog #209228 — a potentially faster-to-browse alternative to the full kirkebok if the full register image set is hard to navigate.

Digitized Hordaland parish registers overall are described by volume_search as 0% name-indexed / not full-text searchable for the 1750-1821 period — they must be browsed page by page at Digitalarkivet or via the FamilySearch Catalog film images.

Probate for this area was handled by the Nordhordaland sorenskriveri/fogderi (skifteprotokoller 1702-1910, FamilySearch Catalog #438738), except farms belonging to the Lysekloster estate, whose probates were kept under Hardanger og Voss.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Hamre prestegjeld (Meland and Hammer/Hamre parishes), Hordaland (1750-1821)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Hamre prestegjeld (clerical district) covered the parishes of Hamre (Hammer), Meland, Alversund and Åsane with Salhus chapel through the target period; Meland and Alversund were not separated into their own clerical district until 1885. Civil county: Hordaland (Nordre Bergenhus amt / Søndre Bergenhus amt, 1763-1919); diocese: Bjørgvin; deanery (prosti): Åsane prosti; probate/court jurisdiction: Nordhordaland sorenskriveri.
- **County seat / administrative center:** Bergen (city, administered separately from Hordaland county).
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Hordaland County, Norway (merged into Vestland county in 2020, per Wikipedia).
- **Population during period:** No FamilySearch population-tool data could be retrieved for Meland specifically ("No population data found"); the 1801 Norway census (Digitalarkivet/FamilySearch collection 3733603) lists Hamre/Meland households directly and is the closest contemporary population source.
- **Economy:** Rural farming parishes on islands/fjords north of Bergen; farm-based agriculture (see Farm Names list on the Hamre Parish wiki page).
- **Ethnic composition:** Not addressed by any tool result for this period; not reported here.
- **Religious denominations:** State Lutheran church only — Norway was Lutheran by law from the 1536 Reformation, and non-Lutheran worship (Catholic, Quaker) was illegal or tightly restricted until 1845 (FamilySearch Wiki, Norway Church Records: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Church_Records).
- **Key historical events:** None specific to this locality surfaced by the tools for 1750-1821.

## Boundary changes
- Meland and Hammer (Hamre) parishes, and Alversund, were part of a single Hamre clerical district (prestegjeld) throughout 1750-1821; Hosanger, Mo and Seim had already split off in 1749, just before the target period. The Hamre/Meland/Alversund grouping held until 1885, when Meland and Alversund became their own Alversund clerical district (FamilySearch Wiki, Hamre Parish: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Hamre_Parish,_Hordaland,_Norway_Genealogy).
- Practical effect: a marriage between an Anders Monsen of Meland and an Unna Halsteinsdatter of Hammer parish in this period would be recorded in the SAME kirkebok (Hamre prestegjeld register), not two separate parish books — this is not a cross-jurisdiction search problem for 1750-1821, unlike it would be after 1885.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Norway had no secular civil registration of births/marriages/deaths in this period — these events were recorded only in state Lutheran church (parish-level) registers. A uniform church-record form was introduced by royal ordinance in December 1812, used from winter 1814, replaced in 1820 (FamilySearch Wiki, Norway Church Records: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Church_Records). Civil registration proper came much later and is out of this period's scope.
- **What exists:** See Church records below — the parish register IS the vital record for this period.
- **Where held:** Parish level (kirkebok), later transferred to state archives (Statsarkivet i Bergen) after 80 years.
- **Gaps:** Pre-1812 entries follow no standard form and vary in completeness; no indexed online marriage collection narrows below the full-register browse for this specific parish/period (see Church records).

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** State Lutheran only (see Jurisdiction overview).
- **Record types:** Baptisms/christenings (døpte), marriages (viede/vigde/copulerede, sometimes a separate earlier engagement/trolovelse entry), burials (begravede), confirmations (from 1736), vaccination notes, arrival/removal lists (mostly 1814-1875).
- **Where held:** The core source is "Kirkebøker, 1677-1928," Hamre prestegjeld (Hordaland), FamilySearch Catalog #47267 — images, covering Hamre (Hammer), Meland, Alversund, Åsane/Salhus for this period. Digitalarkivet holds the same material as browsable scanned image sets, specifically labeled "Hamre/Alversund, Hamre, Hosanger, Meland, Mo, Seim Parish Church Records 1677-1750" and "Hamre/Alversund, Hamre, Meland Parish Church Records 1750-1857" (https://media.digitalarkivet.no/kb/browse?archives%5B%5D=no-a1450-07000000000996). A separate extract, "Hamre/Alversund, Hamre, Hosanger, Meland, Mo, Seim ... extract of the christenings and marriages, 1677-1826," is at FamilySearch Catalog #209228 — potentially a faster-to-browse condensed version.
- **Gaps:** `volume_search` found no record of this Hamre series as fulltext-searchable or indexed for 1750-1821 — it (like essentially all Hordaland parish registers for this window) is browse-only images, 0% name-indexed. Per `collections_search`/wiki, the broad FamilySearch "Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926" index (collection 1468080) and "Norway, Church Books, 1797-1958" (collection 4237104) may surface an index entry for this marriage if it was transcribed, but coverage for pre-1797/pre-indexed years cannot be assumed — treat these as a first-pass index check, with the full Hamre kirkebok image browse as the authoritative fallback.
- **Language:** Danish/Norwegian (Gothic handwriting); Norwegian Genealogical Word List and handwriting guides are linked from the Norway Research Tips page.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** 1801 Norway Census (FamilySearch collection 3733603 / Digitalarkivet, index & images, includes Hamre/Meland) is within the target window and names households by farm. The next national census after that for this area is 1865 — outside the 1750-1821 window.
- **State/provincial census:** Local/parish-level folketellinger exist for neighboring Hordaland prestegjeld in 1815, 1825, 1835, 1845 (per FamilySearch Catalog hits, e.g. koha:701507 "1835 folketelling for Hamre prestegjeld," koha:701516 "1845 folketelling for Hamre prestegjeld") — the 1835 and 1845 Hamre-prestegjeld counts explicitly list Åsane, Hamre (Hammer), Meland and Alversund together, confirming the shared-register point above, though these two postdate 1821 slightly for the 1835/45 rolls.
- **Other enumerations:** 1664-1666 and 1701 manntall (men only) exist for Nordhordland fogderi, predating the marriage but useful for the wider family.
- **Access:** 1801 census is indexed and imaged online (Digitalarkivet/FamilySearch). The parish-level 1815-1845 folketellinger are microfilmed in the FamilySearch Catalog (`availableOnline: false` per catalog_search) — physical/microfilm access via FamilySearch Library or affiliate library, not browsable online in this tool's results.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Skifteprotokoller (probate protocols); tingbøker (court minute books).
- **Testate or intestate:** Not established for Anders Monsen or Unna Halsteinsdatter by this survey — unknown.
- **Date range:** Nordhordaland sorenskriveri skifteprotokoller, 1702-1910 (FamilySearch Catalog #438738); a narrower Nordhordaland prosti set covers 1773-1810 (FamilySearch Catalog #438920), squarely inside the target period.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Catalog images, drawn from Statsarkivet i Bergen originals. Note: farms belonging to the Lysekloster estate had their probates kept instead under Hardanger og Voss jurisdiction (FamilySearch Wiki, Hamre Parish page) — check this if a probate is missing from the Nordhordaland set.

## Research tips
- Couples in Norway were usually married in the bride's home parish (FamilySearch Wiki, Norway Church Records: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Church_Records) — search the Hamre prestegjeld register around Hammer/Hestdal (Unna's parish) for the marriage entry first, since both Meland and Hammer fall in the same register for this period.
- Marriage entries before 1814 follow no standard form and vary in content; after 1814 expect bride/groom names, date, residence, marital status, occupation, and named bondsmen — but a pre-1812 entry for this 1750-1821-range marriage (date currently unknown) may be sparse (FamilySearch Wiki, Norway Church Records).
- Because spelling was not standardized before a uniform form (1812/1814), search variant spellings of Anders Monsen, Unna/Una Halsteinsdatter, Håtuft/Haatuft, and Hestdal/Hesdal in both the Digitalarkivet image browse and the FamilySearch "Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926" index.
- Use the Norwegian Genealogical Word List and the Scandinavian Gothic handwriting guide (both linked from the Norway Research Tips and Strategies page: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Research_Tips_and_Strategies) before attempting to read the original kirkebok images.
- Check the Alenfit skibreide farm-history book (covering Hamre, Alversund, Sæbø, Lygra and Seim parish farms to 1814) for independent confirmation of the Håtuft and Hestdal farm families (FamilySearch Wiki, Hamre Parish: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Hamre_Parish,_Hordaland,_Norway_Genealogy).
- If the marriage is not found in the Hamre prestegjeld register, cross-check the 1801 census (collection 3733603) for both households to confirm they are correctly linked to Hamre/Meland before expanding the search elsewhere.
